defects.justification: Gem 'puma' has no version constraint, so bundle install resolves whatever release is newest, including future major versions with breaking changes.
Gem 'sinatra' has no version constraint, so bundle install resolves whatever release is newest, including future major versions with breaking changes.

Gem 'minitest' has no version constraint, so bundle install resolves whatever release is newest, including future major versions with breaking changes.
Gem 'rack-test' has no version constraint, so bundle install resolves whatever release is newest, including future major versions with breaking changes.
request.body.read reads the whole unauthenticated webhook body into memory with no size cap, before the signature is even checked, so a huge POST can exhaust memory.

payment.succeeded only applies to 'pending' orders, so a successful payment that follows a payment.failed (customer retries the card) is recorded as 'ignored' and the order stays 'failed' even though it was paid; the test at webhook_test.rb:77 enshrines this.

The event amount is never compared with the order's stored amount, so a payment.succeeded for any amount (e.g. 1 cent) marks a 1500-cent order 'paid', and a refund of any amount marks it fully 'refunded'.
GET /orders/:id has no authentication, so anyone can look up payment status and amount of any order by guessing ids like 'order-1'.
run! on Sinatra 4 (the unpinned sinatra gem resolves to 4.x) needs the 'rackup' gem to find a server handler, but rackup is not in the Gemfile, so the README's 'bundle exec ruby app.rb' aborts.

The tests never set RACK_ENV/APP_ENV=test, so Sinatra 4.1+ runs in development with host authorization enabled and rejects Rack::Test's default host example.org with 403; the suite fails instead of exercising the app.
